thread:
kevin.choi: :rotating_light: audit-bot flagged cross-tenant accesses from last deployment. can we confirm if the recent rbac migration touched default role scopes?

audit-bot: Alert: policy-change detected on project-scope defaults at 2025-11-03T14:02:11Z. affected_projects=12 affected_orgs=3

maria-g: I reviewed the migration PR #4823 earlier. looks like we accidentally set `default_role.allow_cross_org: true` when normalizing legacy roles.

kevin.choi: ugh. do we know which deploy introduced the change? timestamp on the PR merge?

maria-g: merged at 1759122100 (deploy batch 2025-11-03 13:55 UTC). migration script step: 
```yaml
- name: normalize-default-roles
  set: default_role.allow_cross_org = true
```
I think it was intended to copy existing per-org overrides, not flip the default flag.

dave_ops: found the script run log on infra-runner-7: `rbac_migrate --env=prod --dry=false --apply-defaults` at 1759122125. the env var `RBAC_ASSUME_GLOBAL=false` was missing in the runner config. so migration assumed permissive.

kevin.choi: sounds like a misconfig + bad default. immediate mitigation?

dave_ops: short term: run a corrective migration that sets `default_role.allow_cross_org=false` and applies per-org overrides from backup. command: 
```bash
rbac_migrate --env=prod --apply-fix=revert-default-crossorg --backup=s3://rbac-backups/175912/
```
I'll queue it now in canary region first.

samantha_sec: we should also revoke any active sessions that used cross-org perms and rotate service tokens that were issued during the window. recommend: revoke_sso_tokens --issued-after=1759122100 && rotate_kms_key --alias=rbac-token-signing-key

kevin.choi: do we need full KMS rotation? that has cascade implications (signed URLs, old tokens). maybe targeted rotation of the token signing key only.

samantha_sec: yes only the token-signing CMK. also we need to ensure audit logs capture enough context for retrospection: include `actor_org`, `target_org`, `policy_version` fields. audit-bot can re-export the window to the secure bucket.

audit-bot: Export job queued: export-audit-logs --start=1759122100 --end=1759123500 --dest=s3://security-audit-exports/175912/ status=queued

maria-g: quick vuln triage: did we expose any KMS-wrapped secrets due to this? I checked secrets-service logs — no cross-org secret fetches recorded, only resource-level actions (models, routes).

kevin.choi: ok that's a relief. primary risk is data exfil via model inference requests across org boundary, and incorrect config access.

dave_ops: rollout plan: 
1) canary corrective migration in region us-west-2 (15 min)
2) audit export & confirm no suspicious reads (30 min)
3) global corrective migration with maintenance flag (45 min)
4) token revocation & token-signing-key rotation (20 min)

kevin.choi: who owns step 4? sam?

samantha_sec: I'll own token revocation + KMS rotation. will coordinate with infra to avoid breaking long-lived jobs.

maria-g: I'll prepare the PR to revert the default in the migration script and add a unit test that validates `default_role.allow_cross_org` remains false unless explicitly opt-in.

kevin.choi: logging of action items: @dave_ops run canary fix now, @maria-g open revert PR, @samantha_sec rotate tokens/keys after we confirm canary. post status here once each step done.

dave_ops: starting canary now. tailing logs: `apply-fix: success` 

dave_ops: canary finished. no new cross-org accesses detected in the audit window. proceeding to global.

audit-bot: Export job completed: files=3 size=6.2MB sha256=abcd1234.

kevin.choi: global run completed. no evidence of secret reads. taking system to maintenance briefly to rotate signing key.

samantha_sec: token revocation complete, KMS key rotated (alias rbacs-token-signing-key -> rotated 1759125000). updated config and notified downstream owners.

maria-g: PR merged to add guardrails + test. will add a postmortem doc later with timeline.

kevin.choi: thanks everyone. follow-up items for postmortem: why RBAC_ASSUME_GLOBAL wasn't set on runner, add CI check for migration flags, and ensure audit schema includes actor_org/target_org. marking incident resolved for now :white_check_mark:
